title: Natural additive K-flat computation of universal scalar extension
statement: Let R and B be commutative rings in universe u with an R-algebra structure on B, and derived categories of R- and B-modules with morphisms in universe w [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix an integer i and a quasi-isomorphism f:F to B[0] with F an R-K-flat cochain complex [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Put V=quotient followed by Qh, H=degree-i derived homology, T=the ordinary total tensor bifunctor of R-complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and W=the quasi-isomorphisms in K(R). There is a family of additive equivalences e(L,epsilon,hL,X): H(L(V(X))) to H^i(T(X,F)), for every functor L:D(R) to D(B), counit epsilon:Qh followed by L to ordinary scalar extension followed by Qh, proof hL that this pair is universal, and R-complex X [def-weil-module-base-change]. For every chain map g:X to Y, e at Y sends H(L(V(g)))(x) to H^i(T(g,F))(e at X of x). For two universal pairs (L,epsilon) and (K,delta), let zeta be their canonical leftDerivedNatIso for the identity of the underived scalar extension. Then e(K,delta,X)(H(zeta at V(X))(x))=e(L,epsilon,X)(x). No A-algebra structure, coefficient action, localization unit or mixed tensor occurs in this assertion.

proof.text: Use the actual functorial R-K-flat resolution P(X) -> X from def-pc-ring-tensor-cohomology. K-flatness of F makes P(X) tensor F -> X tensor F a quasi-isomorphism. K-flatness of P(X) makes P(X) tensor F -> P(X) tensor B[0] a quasi-isomorphism. The degree-zero total tensor identification and tensor symmetry identify the latter with restriction to R of the ordinary B-extension of P(X). All identifications use x tensor b -> b tensor x and commute with chain maps.

The universal counit at P(X) is invertible by lem-pc-kflat-scalar-extension-counit. Compose its homology image with the inverse of the derived image of P(X) -> X, the ordinary homology factorization isomorphisms, and the two inverse homology maps in the tensor span. This defines the additive equivalence e for each universal pair and X.

Functorial resolution and counit naturality yield the first equation after cancellation of the invertible span maps. For the second, the canonical isomorphism between universal pairs commutes with their counits by leftDerivedNatTrans_app. Apply it at P(X), take homology, and move its component to X by naturality for P(X) -> X. Cancel the same invertible resolution and tensor maps. The specified orientations yield both displayed pointwise equations.
